Knots Finder Basics About

Best knots for

Camping

Tarps, guy lines, bundles and washing lines. Knots that are quick to tie with cold hands and quick to undo when you pack up.

  • Loops

    Bowline

    The classic fixed loop.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Binding knots

    Clove Hitch

    Two turns round a post with the second crossing over the first.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Splices & whippings

    Common Whipping

    Turns of thin twine bound round a rope end to stop it unravelling.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Hitches

    Cow Hitch

    A bight of rope dropped round a rail with both legs pulled through it.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Loops

    Double Overhand Noose

    A running loop held by a double overhand tied round the standing part.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Bends

    Fisherman’s Knot

    Each end ties an overhand knot round the other rope.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Bends

    Flat Overhand Bend

    The two ends held together and tied as one in an overhand knot.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Hitches

    Half Hitch

    The simplest hitch: the end goes round the standing part and across itself.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Stopper knots

    Overhand Knot

    The simplest knot there is, and the first move of many others.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Hitches

    Round Turn and Two Half Hitches

    A round turn on a ring or post takes the load while you finish with two half hitches round the standing part.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Bends

    Sheet Bend

    The everyday knot for joining two ropes, including ropes of different thickness.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Stopper knots

    Slipped Overhand Knot

    An overhand knot finished with a bight instead of the end, so one pull on the short end releases it.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Binding knots

    Timber Hitch

    A noose that grips a log, a pole or a bundle: the end goes round the standing part and is twisted back round its own turn.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Hitches

    Two Half Hitches

    A turn through a ring or round a post, then two half hitches round the standing part, both the same way.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Bends

    Water Knot

    An overhand knot in one end, followed back through in reverse by the other end.

    ●○○ Easy
  • Loops

    Bowline with Stopper

    A bowline with its tail tied in an overhand knot round the leg of the eye beside it, so the bowline cannot shake loose when it is not loaded..

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Bends

    Double Sheet Bend

    A sheet bend with a second turn of the thinner rope round the bight.

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Loops

    Englishman’s Loop

    A fixed loop made of two overhand knots, one in the end round the standing part and one in the standing part round the end.

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Hitches

    Highwayman’s Hitch

    A quick-release hitch on a rail made only of bights: one bight round the rail, a second through it, and a third through the second.

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Hitches

    Mirrored Rolling Hitch

    The rolling hitch tied as its mirror image, for a pull coming from the opposite side.

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Hitches

    Rolling Hitch

    A hitch that holds against a pull along a pole or another rope, not just across it.

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Lashings

    Sheer Lashing

    Lashes two poles side by side, to lengthen a pole or to make sheer legs (an A-frame).

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Lashings

    Square Lashing

    Lashes two poles that cross at right angles, for frames, tables, gates and trellises.

    ●●○ Intermediate
  • Splices & whippings

    Eye Splice

    A permanent eye in the end of a three-strand rope: the end is bent back and its strands are tucked into the standing part, against the lay.

    ●●● Advanced
